newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees savings boosting profits - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees savings boosting profits - WSJ.

text.p: Chrysler Corp is expected to announce that suppliers have come up with cost-saving measures that would increase 1997 profits by $325 million, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said Chrysler already has received enough ideas from its suppliers to eventually save the automaker a total of $1.2 billion.

"The market is telling us we have to look at internal cost reductions to keep our profits up," said Thomas Stallkamp, executive vice president for procurement and supply. "There is an affordability issue that won't allow us to keep going to our customers with higher prices."
Chrysler spends about $38 billion each year at suppliers for everything from toilet tissue and hand lotion to car seats and brakes.
The company has had a program for the past eight years that asks suppliers to come up with cost-cutting measures that amount to 5 percent of the suppliers' annual sales.
